research.notes:
Scope and method: read all 14 notes (N10-N18, GN06-GN10) in full, then verified concrete file/function/table/line claims against the live gridiron-hq tree via grep/Read (read-only) and one read-only sqlite3 count against the 16GB live DB (nfl_play_by_play row count, N11-3). Also read LATEST-PLAN.md's 'Where things stand right now', 'What a football game HAS/does NOT have', 'Is the ML technique the problem', 'The multiple-testing guardrail', 'Prioritized roadmap' (1446-2397), and 'MODEL INVENTORY AND ORGANIZATION' (2398-2547) in full.

Headline findings for the three notes the task asked to be answered concretely:

N12 (mixture-of-experts council redesign): the answer is RESTRUCTURE, not prune-to-fewer-experts and not leave-as-is — and restructuring is already partially underway independently of N12. At the nfl-ensemble.js layer, the exact defect N12's F1 names (static per-component inverse-RMSE weighting that lets correlated/redundant components keep near-full weight) has been SUPERSEDED: the default weighting path now calls `jointComponentWeights()` (nfl-ensemble.js:1735-1997), a genuine joint ridge regression across every component simultaneously that naturally discounts redundant columns — a different mechanism than N12's proposed Shazeer-style CV² penalty but addressing the same collapse problem, with in-code documentation explicitly citing the old formula's failure and a measured ~1.2-1.4 RMSE point fix. At the nfl-expert-coordinator.js layer, N12's F2 diagnosis (hand-binned discrete regimeLabels() gate, correlation-threshold family merging) remains fully OPEN and unchanged — verified line-for-line against N12's own citations. LATEST-PLAN.md's own newer 'MODEL INVENTORY' section independently reaches the same structural diagnosis as N12 (four duplicate residual predictors, six duplicate combiners, only one path reaches a live pick and it returns the market verbatim) and proposes its own restructuring target (fold everything into forecast-combination.js's existing rigorous combiner) — a genuine alternative mechanism to N12's proposed small jointly-fit MoE gate, flagged in contradictions_with_plan. N12 explicitly does NOT recommend pruning the expert roster size itself, and explicitly warns against a large Shazeer/Switch-scale neural gate given K≈19 experts and only hundreds of games.

N13 (injury network): N13 mis-attributes availability()/weeklyAvailability() to server/services/player-availability.js — they actually live in server/services/contingency.js alongside cascades()/handcuffValue() (wrong_file, N13-1). More importantly, N13 never discusses server/services/nfl-availability.js at all — the file that is actually wired into the NFL spread forecast (nfl-ensemble.js's sharedContext.avail and calibrate()'s per-week availability differential, imported at nfl-ensemble.js:25) and that LATEST-PLAN.md documents as the signal that measured null this session ('Correction head V2 (+availability/PFR defense): 9.943, +0.030 vs V1 — not significant'). nfl-availability.js is single-hop, team-level, snap-share × status × positional-or-PFR-production weighted — it has none of N13's prescribed multi-hop cross-position propagation, backup-specific scheme-fit conditioning, or correlated-injury interaction terms. N13's own candidates are almost all labeled applies_to:fantasy and scoped to contingency.js/nfl-player-value.js's handcuff-ranking use case, not explicitly to the betting model's nfl-availability.js signal — extending F1 (protection-degradation graph feeding team-strength) and N1 (two-hop cascade) to nfl-availability.js's team-level deficit, not only to the fantasy handcuff layer, is the concrete extension the spread model needs and that N13 itself does not make explicit (N13-6).

N17 (weather/venue causal): compared against the plan's own 'Creative sweep' findings (LATEST-PLAN.md:2171-2201), which independently discovered the same unused nfl_stadiums altitude/lat/lon/timezone data N17's candidate 3 targets, and scheduled it as roadmap item 10 alongside surface-type and coaching-continuity gaps N17 does not cover. N17's candidate 5 (per-team empirical-Bayes-shrunk weather sensitivity replacing the flat constants) has ALREADY SHIPPED as weatherSensitivity()/weatherAdjustment() in nfl-ensemble.js:536-660, with more rigorous methodology (synthetic-null-calibrated significance gate) than N17 itself proposed — a clean 'done' finding. N17's candidates 1 (fixed-effects panel regression to replace the flat FLAT_WEATHER_POINTS constants themselves), 2 (humidity/pressure ingestion), and 4 (wind-surprise signal) remain fully open and unbuilt.

Other high-value findings surfaced along the way, beyond the three prioritized notes: N14's F1 (unify devig behind exchangeVsBook via Shin's method) has shipped (prediction-markets.js:170-280, bookMoneylineNoVig()); the CLV-implementation fragmentation N14/N18 both flag has been consolidated into clv-core.js ('Giant Plan 8.1', nfl-clv.js deleted outright); N15's headline finding (nfl_play_formations discards 6 real route/coverage columns from an already-downloaded CSV, plus a stale 'participation ends after 2023' comment) is fully confirmed and still open; N16/GN10's dynasty-age-curve.js critique is fully confirmed and still open.

Given the volume of concrete claims across 14 dense notes (each naming dozens of files/functions/lines), this item list is a substantial but representative sample (77 items) rather than an exhaustive one-item-per-sentence enumeration — coverage is deepest for N12/N13/N17 as instructed, with solid representative coverage of every other note's most load-bearing, independently-checkable claims.

architecture_prescriptions: [glickman_stern_1998] Team strength should be modeled as a first-order autoregressive state-space process with two separate variance components — week-to-week (within-season) and season-to-season (between-season) — plus a home-field-advantage term allowed to vary by team; the paper's own such model beat the Las Vegas line on the last 110 games of the 1993 season.

[glickman_2001_dpcmsv] Team-strength state variance should itself be allowed to evolve stochastically (not fixed), with an AR(1) mean-reversion term (q<1) toward zero between seasons, fit by MCMC/Kalman-type filtering; this captures sudden shifts (e.g. a team collapsing) that a constant-variance dynamic model smooths over.

[szczecinski_tihon_2021_kf] A rating engine should be derived as an approximate Kalman filter from an explicit pair of probabilistic models — (1) how skill maps to game outcome, (2) how skill evolves over time — rather than adopting a fixed ad hoc update rule; Elo, Glicko and TrueSkill are all shown to be special cases of this one general recursive Bayesian update.

[lopez_matthews_baumer_2018] A cross-sport-comparable rating system should be a Bayesian state-space model fit on betting-market data (not just outcomes), decomposing team-strength variance into between-season, within-season, and game-to-game components plus a home-advantage term, so 'how much of the outcome is luck' becomes an explicit, estimated quantity rather than assumed.

[koopman_lit_2012_dbp] For totals/scoring, a dynamic bivariate Poisson model with stochastically time-varying attack/defense intensities (state-space + importance sampling) is the prescribed shape, not a static Poisson fit; the paper's own implementation produced a statistically significant positive return over bookmaker odds out-of-sample.

[koopman_lit_2019_gas] Among score-driven (GAS) specifications keyed to three possible observables (paired goal counts, the count difference, or win/loss/draw), the pairwise-count GAS model gives the most precise forecasts while the difference-count GAS model is the most profitable for betting — both beat benchmark and competing models; informational content is highest for the full pairwise-count representation, so it should be the base observable where feasible.

[dm-1995] Forecast-accuracy comparison must be done with a test that (a) allows an arbitrary, non-quadratic economic loss function and (b) uses a HAC-adjusted standard error built from the loss differential's own autocovariances, because forecast errors used for real decisions are routinely non-Gaussian, serially correlated (k-1 dependence at a k-step horizon) and contemporaneously correlated — a plain paired t-test on per-observation squared error is invalid whenever any of those hold.

[dm-20yrs-later] The DM test was designed and should be used for comparing already-produced FORECASTS, not for comparing MODELS via pseudo-out-of-sample splits; for model (as opposed to forecast) comparison, simpler full-sample procedures exist, are more powerful, and 'have been, and should continue to be, widely used' — pseudo-out-of-sample analysis is not automatically the best or only defense against overfitting in model comparison.

[giacomini-white-2006] Forecast evaluation should test CONDITIONAL predictive ability — whether one forecasting METHOD (model + its parameter-estimation procedure, including what data/window was used to fit it) beats another given information available at forecast time — not just the unconditional average-loss comparison DM/West-style tests give; this is required to properly evaluate estimated (not fixed) forecasting procedures and to compare nested models, which unconditional tests cannot do validly.

[beggy_kelly] Full Kelly staking is not viable in a realistic betting environment (100% simulated bankruptcy rate in the paper's study); a fractional-Kelly stake with coefficient ~0.50 combined with a conservative minimum-edge threshold (~10%) is the recommended sizing rule, trading some growth rate for survival.

[lei] Split-conformal (and full-conformal) prediction intervals give finite-sample, distribution-free marginal coverage for ANY point/quantile estimator with no distributional assumptions, at the cost of only marginal (not conditional) coverage guarantees; the same framework yields a model-free variable-importance measure (LOCO) as a byproduct.

[limits] Exact distribution-free CONDITIONAL coverage (valid for every individual test point, not just on average) is provably impossible without further assumptions; the achievable middle ground is a relaxed notion such as coverage conditional on a partition of the feature space (Mondrian-style grouping) — calibration should therefore explicitly bin/group by a known-in-advance feature rather than claim true pointwise conditional coverage.

[cqr] Interval width should be adaptive to heteroscedasticity by conformalizing quantile regression (fit low/high quantile functions, then conformally correct them) rather than using a single global or per-bin dispersion estimate, which produces intervals of constant or weakly-varying length across the input space and is provably less efficient when true uncertainty varies with the inputs.

[enbpi] For sequential/time-series prediction, interval construction should avoid the i.i.d.-exchangeability assumption entirely and instead wrap an ensemble of predictors (leave-one-out style) to produce intervals without retraining at every step, which conformal methods built on exchangeable calibration sets cannot do validly under a changing time-series distribution.

[nexcp / aci] Under distribution shift, coverage should be maintained either by re-weighting the calibration set (heavier weight on recent/relevant points, with a symmetrized nonexchangeable threshold) or by online-updating a single miscoverage parameter (alpha_t) based on realized coverage so far, so that long-run coverage is guaranteed irrespective of the true (unknown, shifting) data-generating process — a static, unweighted calibration set is the wrong tool once the environment is known to drift (rule changes, pace, market efficiency changes across NFL seasons).
contradictions_with_plan: dm-20yrs-later (Diebold 2012) explicitly argues DM-type pseudo-out-of-sample tests are for comparing forecasts, not for adjudicating between models, and that simpler full-sample procedures 'should continue to be, widely used' for model comparison -- yet LATEST-PLAN.md's 'MODEL INVENTORY AND ORGANIZATION' section makes DM-gating (via `dieboldMariano`/HLN, `dmAlpha: 0.05`) the exclusive promotion mechanism across the whole L3 gate layer (the residual gate, the forecast-combination promotion gate, the effective-rank work), with no full-sample alternative considered anywhere in the roadmap.

giacomini-white-2006's central prescription -- test CONDITIONAL predictive ability of the forecasting METHOD (model + estimation window), not just unconditional average loss -- is identified by this project's own F02 note (docs/betting-model/research/advanced-methods-and-github/F02-forecast-combination.md:94-150) as a concrete, cheap extension ('swap scalar ΔL for h_t·ΔL_t, use a proper HAC Ω̂') with a named attachment point. LATEST-PLAN.md's roadmap and 'Where things stand right now' section list this only as unread/unexecuted corpus content, not as a scheduled roadmap item -- the plan's L3/L4 layers (gridiron-model.js AUTHORITY ladder, nfl-replay.js) are described purely in terms of unconditional DM/bootstrap gates.

Glickman-Stern (1998), Glickman (2001), and Szczecinski-Tihon (2021) all prescribe that team-strength ratings themselves be produced by a formal dynamic state-space/Kalman-filter process with explicit variance decomposition and derived (not ad hoc) update rules. LATEST-PLAN.md's 'MODEL INVENTORY AND ORGANIZATION' table instead classifies all rating sources (`nfelo.js`, `nfl-team-strength.js`, `nfl-external-ratings.js`) as row 8, 'Rating inputs... Inputs to 1 and 3, not stacks' -- i.e. flat feature inputs to be registered in the L1 signal registry, with no roadmap item proposing to rebuild the rating-generation process itself as a Kalman/state-space model; the closest match (roadmap item 8a, cross-sectional James-Stein shrinkage on `nfl-preseason-blend.js`) is a static empirical-Bayes shrinkage, not the papers' dynamic AR(1)/stochastic-variance construction.

items.claim: Team strength in NFL games should be estimated with a dynamic paired-comparison state-space model whose variance is itself allowed to change stochastically over time (not held constant), fit with a filtering algorithm derived for large numbers of objects; on 1996-2000 NFL data this stochastic-variance model produced materially different (and more responsive) team-strength posteriors than a constant-variance dynamic model.
items.evidence: nfl-preseason-blend.js:14-16 implements only a static normal-normal Bayesian shrink (fixed sigma^2/tau^2 posterior weight, re-derived per game count) between a prior-season rating and current-season results -- not an AR(1) state-space model with a stochastic (time-varying) state variance. nfl-team-strength.js:1-45 aggregates offseason/roster features, not a paired-comparison dynamic model. No MCMC/Kalman filtering of team strength with stochastic variance exists anywhere in server/services/*.js (grep for 'kalman'/'state.space'/'stochastic variance' returns nothing outside conformal.js and this note's own text).
items.recommended_action: None planned currently; would require building an actual AR(1)/stochastic-variance state-space fit for team strength rather than the current single-parameter normal-normal shrink in nfl-preseason-blend.js.

items.evidence: nfl-preseason-blend.js:1-51 documents a season-boundary blend (prior season vs. current season) calibrated as a single normal-normal posterior weight, with no explicit week-to-week AR(1) evolution within a season, no team-varying HFA estimated jointly with strength, and no MCMC/Kalman fit. nfl-market.js's fitModel() (per F11-conformal-calibration.md:9-15, corroborated by conformal.js integration at nfl-market.js:205-226) computes a single pooled residual SD off a static regression, not a dynamic state-space margin model.

items.claim: Comparing two forecasters' accuracy requires a test that (a) allows an arbitrary, non-quadratic loss function and (b) uses a spectral/HAC-consistent standard error built from the loss differential's own autocovariances (accommodating non-Gaussian, non-zero-mean, serially and contemporaneously correlated forecast errors) rather than the naive large-sample-normal or paired-t comparison of point accuracy estimates.
items.evidence: server/services/forecast-comparison.js:228 exports `dieboldMariano()` implementing exactly this HAC-based test (module docstring at forecast-comparison.js:1-49 explicitly cites Diebold & Mariano 1995 and derives the exact-identity relationship to the paired t at horizon 1). server/services/nfl-ensemble.js:1909 calls `dieboldMariano(modelLoss, marketLoss, {horizon:1, clusters: scoreWeekLabels})` in production gating. backtest-significance.js:57 implements a complementary paired-bootstrap (not DM itself) also citing the need for dependence-aware comparison.

items.claim: The DM test is designed for comparing already-produced FORECASTS, not for comparing MODELS in a pseudo-out-of-sample setting; for model comparison, simpler and more compelling full-sample procedures exist and should continue to be used -- pseudo-out-of-sample analysis is not automatically the best defense against over-fitting.

items.claim: Forecast evaluation should test CONDITIONAL predictive ability of the forecasting METHOD (model plus estimation procedure/window), using inference about conditional rather than unconditional expectations of forecast errors, and should be valid under heterogeneity and for both nested and non-nested model comparisons -- an explicit generalization of the West (1996)/DM unconditional-test framework.
items.evidence: grep for 'giacomini'/'conditional predictive ability' across server/ and research/ returns zero hits in code; only docs/betting-model/research/advanced-methods-and-github/F02-forecast-combination.md:94-150 and FIX_AND_ADD_ARCHITECTURE.md:80 reference it as a read-but-unbuilt idea, with F02 naming a concrete attachment point ('replace the ad hoc paired-t at nfl-ensemble.js:1125-1129 with this exact statistic, extended to the Giacomini-White conditional form'). items.claim: Full Kelly staking is not viable in realistic betting conditions (100% simulated bankruptcy rate); a fractional-Kelly stake with coefficient ~0.50 plus a conservative ~10% minimum-edge threshold is the recommended sizing rule, and it produced an ~80% annualized return over an 11-year backtest.

Full (unfractional) Kelly is not used anywhere in the live staking path (grep confirms `kellyFraction` calls always pass an explicit `fraction` < 1).

items.claim: Split-conformal (and full-conformal) prediction wraps any point estimator to give finite-sample, distribution-free MARGINAL coverage guarantees with no distributional assumptions, and the same machinery yields a model-free variable-importance measure (LOCO, leave-one-covariate-out).

items.claim: Conformalized Quantile Regression (fit low/high quantile functions, then conformally correct their coverage) gives intervals that adapt to heteroscedasticity, producing shorter intervals than fixed-width or coarsely-binned conformal methods.

items.claim: Conformal prediction under distribution shift/non-exchangeability should use WEIGHTED quantiles (heavier weight on more relevant/recent points) combined with a randomization technique for nonsymmetric algorithms, achieving substantially better coverage under drift than standard exchangeable conformal, while reducing to standard conformal when data are in fact exchangeable.

items.claim: Exact distribution-free CONDITIONAL coverage (valid for every individual point, not just on average) is provably impossible without additional distributional assumptions; the practically achievable relaxation is coverage conditional on a partition of the feature space (grouped/'Mondrian' conformal prediction).
items.evidence: conformal.js:24-34 explicitly implements exactly this relaxation ('Mondrian binning is the conditional half... Binning the calibration set by a feature known before kickoff... gives per-bin coverage instead... The guarantee survives binning because conformal prediction only needs exchangeability within each bin, not across bins' -- this is a correct paraphrase of the paper's own recommended approach), implemented via binIndex()/buildConformal() at conformal.js:41-140.
items.recommended_action: None -- correctly implemented as the paper's own prescribed relaxation of exact conditional coverage.

items.claim: Under unknown/time-varying distribution shift, a single miscoverage parameter (alpha_t) should be online-updated based on realized coverage so far, provably achieving the target long-run coverage frequency irrespective of the true (shifting) data-generating process, as a general wrapper around any point/quantile predictor.
items.evidence: No online/adaptive alpha-updating loop exists anywhere in the codebase (grep for 'alpha_t'/'adaptive.*alpha'/'realized coverage'/'online.*coverage' in server/services/*.js returns no matches). conformal.js's calibration is refit per walk-forward step on a static historical pool (buildConformal(), conformal.js:81), not adjusted online based on tracked realized coverage. LATEST-PLAN.md's MODEL INVENTORY GitHub-mapping (line ~2384) lists 'aangelopoulos/conformal-time-series ACI correction (#27), only after a base interval is tracked live' as explicitly deferred/open.
items.recommended_action: Matches LATEST-PLAN.md's own deferred item: build ACI-style online alpha correction only after a base conformal interval is tracked live in production, as the plan already schedules.

research.notes: Scope note: this pass covers the 16 primary source papers (6 in source-papers/papers/*.txt, 4 in source-papers/research2/*.pdf via Read, 6 conformal papers in source-papers/pdfs/*.txt), verified against the live tree by grep/Read only -- no files were edited. Three of the research2 PDFs (mdpi_rl_survey.pdf, rl_trading_survey_2212.pdf, zhang_zohren_rl_trading.pdf) were present in research2/ but were NOT in the task's named list (dm-1995, dm-20yrs-later, giacomini-white-2006, beggy_kelly) and so were not read or scored as items -- flagging in case the RL-trading surveys were meant to be included; they are out of scope for the NFL spread/totals betting model per the task's own file list. Key overall finding: the conformal-prediction family is the most mature relative to its papers (Mondrian split-conformal, the 'limits' paper's own prescribed relaxation, is fully implemented and wired into both nfl-market.js and nfl-ensemble.js); the dynamic-rating-model family (Glickman/Stern, Glickman 2001, Szczecinski-Tihon, Koopman-Lit) is uniformly unimplemented -- every rating/team-strength file in the repo uses static or single-parameter-shrink methods, never a fitted state-space/Kalman/GAS process, which is the single largest gap between what these papers prescribe and what LATEST-PLAN.md's current architecture builds. Diebold-Mariano/HLN is correctly and thoroughly implemented (forecast-comparison.js), but its extension to Giacomini-White's conditional form -- already scoped with a file/line attachment point in this project's own F02 note -- remains unbuilt, and the plan does not currently distinguish 'comparing forecasts' from 'comparing models' the way dm-20yrs-later insists it must.
